Handshake.description: How long a replacement native server may take to answer the gateway's initialize handshake before the refresh is abandoned: the candidate is stopped and the serving server stays.

DiscoveryHold.description: How long the gateway holds a discovery request (tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list) while a native server is being started, so the client receives the real lists in the reply instead of empty ones it may never refetch. It stays well below a client's connect and request timeouts. Past the bound, or when no native server can be ready soon, the empty lists of WarmDiscovery answer and list_changed follows.

Refresh.description: How a gateway that already serves a usable published native server treats the background refresh: a failed refresh is logged and serving continues, an unchanged refresh does nothing, a changed refresh swaps a freshly handshaken server in for new requests while the replaced server finishes the requests it already holds (its own requests and notifications are forwarded under gateway-unique request ids so both servers can mint the same ids, a stale response is dropped with the logged line, the client's logging level, resource subscriptions and roots change are replayed to the new server before it takes over, and a replaced server that exits early fails the requests it still held).

const.droppedFrame: [semio-os-mcp] dropped a frame from a replaced server

Supervision.description: How a gateway treats an unexpected exit of the serving native server while it is ready (non-zero status or a signal; a clean exit and a client close are not crashes): its held requests are answered with a retryable JSON-RPC error (code -32603, data.cause server-exited, the exit and the en + de summary, `{exit}` is replaced by `status N` or `signal NAME`), a replacement server is started through the refresh handshake and replay path while the staging continues, requests arriving meanwhile queue and the replacement announces list_changed. At most maximumRestarts restarts (crashes and replacements that failed their handshake) are made within windowMilliseconds; beyond that the session fails as for a clean server loss.

const.restartingPrefix: [semio-os-mcp] the native server exited unexpectedly, restarting it:
const.exhaustedPrefix: [semio-os-mcp] the native server keeps exiting, giving up:
const.message: the native server exited with {exit}; the request was not completed and may be retried

summary.en: The native server exited with {exit} and is restarting; the request was not completed, retry it.
summary.de: Der native Server wurde mit {exit} beendet und startet neu; die Anfrage wurde nicht abgeschlossen, bitte erneut senden.

Models.description: How a gateway that relays a typed missing-model refusal from the serving native server (schema 📦️component-models, definition MissingModel) reacts: it asks its launcher to build that plugin's component model once per plugin and session (one build at a time, cancelled with the session), logs the stages with these prefixes, and, when the launcher published a changed model set, swaps a freshly handshaken server in behind the client, which sees the model through its environment. A failed build is logged, remembered with its reason and retried by the next refusal; until a build succeeds every relayed refusal of that plugin is rewritten so the client reads the truth (cause `model-build-failed`, the reason, en + de summary with `{pluginId}` and `{reason}` replaced, at most `maximumReasonCharacters` of the reason) instead of the promise that the launcher is preparing it.

const.preparingPrefix: [semio-os-mcp] building the component model of plugin

failedSummary.en: Plugin `{pluginId}` has no component model: its last build failed ({reason}); the launcher is building it again, retry in a moment.
failedSummary.de: Das Plugin `{pluginId}` hat kein Komponentenmodell: der letzte Bau ist fehlgeschlagen ({reason}); der Starter baut es erneut, gleich erneut versuchen.

WarmDiscovery.description: The answers to discovery while no native server can be ready within DiscoveryHold, or once that bound passed: empty lists, because a client bounds discovery by its request timeout and staging can outlast it. The native catalog replaces them through the list_changed notifications the gateway announces once the native server is ready.

ClientReadiness.description: How long a client of a warming gateway waits for the native catalog announcement (notifications/tools/list_changed) before it gives up: a cold checkout provisions dependencies and compiles the native server first.
